topic: BC Cancer Lung Screening Program reporting (BC Lung Screening Protocol v2.0, January 2026)
today: Not on the site. Program LDCTs in BC are reported with the PanCan risk score at baseline, volumetry and VDT at follow-up and categories 1–5 with different intervals (1: 2 years, 2: 1 year, 3: 3 months, 4–5: referral); the site has nothing on it. Its place depends on the lead choice (B1-lung-rads-01).

topic: PanCan (Brock / McWilliams) nodule malignancy risk calculator
today: Not on the site. Sets the BC program's baseline category (p15) and Lung-RADS v2022 note 13 encourages it for 4B; no calculator on the site.

Not on the site. Lung-RADS v2022 note 15 points to the ACR incidental-findings guidance and LCS quick guide; the BC program has its own table with thresholds (pp16–17). The page has only four unsourced S examples.

Not on the site. ACR (in-press PDF p5) gives the protocol its thresholds depend on: reduced-dose unenhanced CT over the adrenals at 120 kVp read in real time, contrast-enhanced at 60–90 s, 15-minute delay, 3 mm axial and coronal. The page has only a "10–15 min delay" label.

topic: Tiebreaking rules and "if unsure, characterize a major feature as absent"

topic: How to measure size and when threshold growth applies
today: Not on the site. Core p.20: outer edge to outer edge including capsule, not on arterial phase or DWI if margins are clear elsewhere; threshold growth only for a definite mass against prior CT/MRI. Not on the page.
Not on the site. Core p.6 and p.16, ch8 p.8-6: report the path diagnosis instead of a category (except regenerative or dysplastic nodules). Not on the page.

Not on the site. Core p.3 lists surveillance US and CEUS algorithms beside CT/MRI; the site covers only CT/MRI. Owner to decide whether they belong.

topic: CT technique for nodules (thin sections, reformats, low-dose follow-up, comparison with the earliest prior)
today: Fleischner 2017 gives graded recommendations (≤ 1.5 mm contiguous sections, typically 1 mm, with coronal and sagittal series; low-dose follow-up, CTDIvol ≤ 3 mGy in a standard-size patient; review priors including the earliest; journal pp230–232); the page has none.

topic: Nodules that need no follow-up (benign calcification, fat, typical intrapulmonary lymph node, apical scarring, 2-year stability)
today: Fleischner Figs 1, 2 and 5 (journal pp231, 233), stopping follow-up of benign-looking solid nodules stable at 12–18 months (p233), apical scarring (p240); the Choosing Wisely Canada 2026 recommendation 1 (abstract) says the same. The page has only the perifissural line and the calculator has no benign exit.

topic: Nodules on incomplete thoracic CT (neck, cardiac, abdominal CT)
today: Fleischner journal p240: < 6 mm, nothing further; 6–8 mm, complete chest CT at 3–12 months; large or very suspicious, complete chest CT now; partial thoracic scans not recommended for follow-up. Common on call; not on the page.

topic: Reporting incidental nodules (always give a recommendation, compare with the earliest scan)
today: Choosing Wisely Canada 2026 recommendations 2 and 4 (abstract only) and the Canadian expert-panel consensus (Digby 2024, CARJ; abstract only) call for standardized reports with follow-up advice for every size band; the page has no reporting guidance.

topic: Prostate MRI after treatment (suspected local recurrence)
today: PI-RADS v2.1 does not apply after treatment (pp. 3, 24) and the page only says prior treatment "may alter assessment" (B2-pi-rads-34); nothing on the site covers recurrence reporting (CAR cites PI-RR, ref 23).
PI-RADS v2.1 does not address progression during surveillance (p. 3); CAR cites the PRECISE recommendations (ref 31); no page covers it.
CAR recommends reporting image quality and auditing 10 cases every 6 months (Table 1, recommendations 1–2; Appendix G adapted from PI-QUAL); the page has no image-quality item.

topic: Incidental thyroid nodules on CT, MRI and PET/CT
today: TI-RADS covers nodules on ultrasound; whether an incidental nodule on other imaging needs an ultrasound is a separate ACR white paper (Hoang et al., JACR 2015;12:143-50, the white paper's ref 9), and the site has no page for it.

topic: Thyroid nodules in children and adolescents
today: ACR TI-RADS is for adults (white paper p2); the page sets its line at 14 years and nothing on the site covers younger patients.

topic: Contrast switching after a hypersensitivity reaction
today: CAR/CSACI 2025 (Rec 3, Figure 1) make switching to a chemically different agent the single best protective measure for ICM and GBCA; the ACR also describes changing agents within a class (p10, PDF p13). The page never mentions it.

topic: Prior reaction to an unknown iodinated agent
today: CAR/CSACI 2025 Rec 4 and Figure 2 (before 2000: give LOCM without premedication; from 2000: by severity), updated by the 2025 CAR/CSACI unknown-agent paper, which is not readable yet.

topic: Delayed and severe reactions: premedication, allergy referral, tryptase
today: CAR/CSACI: no premedication for delayed reactions (p6); allergy referral after severe reactions including SJS/TEN or DRESS (p9); serum tryptase 30–120 minutes after anaphylaxis onset (Rec 11).

topic: Other acute reactions in ACR Table 3, and children (Table 2)
today: The page lacks diffuse erythema, hypertensive crisis, pulmonary edema, seizures, hypoglycemia, anxiety and reaction-rebound prevention, and gives adult doses without saying so; children have weight-based doses in ACR Table 2.
CAR/CSACI Rec 13: patients should not be told to fast unless the examination requires it; the ACR has a fasting chapter (p13, PDF p16).

topic: CA-AKI screening, repeat contrast and follow-up creatinine
today: CAR 2022 Rec 1–2 (screening questions; inpatient eGFR within 7 days; no delay for emergent studies), Rec 7 (repeat contrast within 48 hours only restricted for elective studies in higher-risk patients), Rec 20 (creatinine at 48–72 hours only after IA contrast with eGFR ≤30).

ACR–ASNR position statement on gadolinium deposition (p70, PDF p73) and CAR/CSACI Rec 6 and 9 (prior GBCA reaction: no steroids, switch agent); the page covers neither. Whether CAR 2018/2019 cover retention is unknown until they are read.

Not on the site. BI-RADS v2025 makes CEM an intrinsic section with its own lexicon (what’s-new p. 1 and p. 8) and CAR published a 2026 CEM guideline (part II, cited as ref 1 in car-breast-1-2026, not downloaded); the site has nothing on CEM.

topic: CT-FFR and CT perfusion (the I modifier)

topic: Stents and bypass grafts on CCTA
today: Not on the site. CAR Part 1 p. 495 (stents >3 mm assessable; CABG coverage) and SCCT 2026 pp. 468-470 (in-stent restenosis grading, graft reporting) have no home on the site.

Not on the site. CAR gives 5–15% oversizing as generally preferred (p. 506; EACVI e218: 8–14%, rarely >20%); the page says nothing about oversizing or annular rupture risk (SCCT 2019: >20% oversizing and calcium within 2 mm below the annulus, under the non-coronary cusp).
Not on the site. SCCT 2019 (Landing zone calcium; Table 5, strong) and ESCR (Table 5) ask for annular and sub-annular calcium graded and located; the page only mentions it inside the bicuspid box.

Not on the site. CAR (p. 506: systolic sizing phase, coverage from the subclavian arteries to the lesser trochanter) and SCCT 2019 (Tables 1–3: no nitroglycerin, no routine beta blockade, >250 HU, reconstruction ≤1 mm) are not on the page, which points to the old protocols site instead.

topic: Aortic valve calcium score in discordant or low-gradient aortic stenosis
today: Not on the site. SCCT 2019 (Non-contrast cardiac CT: Agatston ≥3000 men / ≥1600 women makes severe AS very likely; <1600 / <800 unlikely) and CAR (p. 507) describe it; it may belong on the valve grading page rather than here.

Not on the site. SCCT 2019 Table 9 lists the report items (incl. image quality and phase, annular area and perimeter, LM and RCA heights, mean sinus, STJ, access findings by femoral-head level); the page has no reporting section.

topic: Post-TTVR CT (device position, leaflet thickening and valve thrombosis)
today: Not on the site. The page stops at planning. Hausleiter 2025 uses CT after implantation for device position, leaflet morphology and complications (p. 272; Figure 7, p. 278: HALT after Evoque; Figure 10, p. 284: valve thrombosis at 2 months); scct-prosthetic-valves-2025 covers transcatheter valves in all positions (not checked here for the tricuspid).

topic: Post-LAAO CT (peri-device leak, device-related thrombus, position)
today: Not on the site. The page has no post-procedure section. CAR Part 2 names post-procedural CT (p. 509); SCAI/HRS 2023 recommends TEE or CT at 45–90 days (recommendation 12) and the 2025 SCAI/HRS guideline suggests TEE or CT after LAAO (recommendation 6.1); EACVI advises TOE surveillance at 45–90 days (pp. 406–407). Korsholm 2024 (the CT position statement) is not readable yet.

topic: RVSP from the tricuspid regurgitant jet
today: Not on the site. The calculators index card for this calculator promises "TR jet → RVSP estimation", but the Bernoulli page has none. EAE/ASE 2009 Table 8 (p. 17) gives sPAP = 4v²tricuspid + RA pressure. Whether the converter should offer it, with an RA pressure input, is a stage 3 choice; the valve-grading page's RVSP and RAP lines are audited there.
